text:
Theo (AE): MedBridge wants a concise preflight for Private install — they asked specifically about drivers, supported CUDA, and what we need from their network/security team. Can we put together a short checklist they can run and paste back output?

Priya (SE): I'll draft. Quick Q: will they accept a temporary installer token or require our engineers on a jump host?

Nina - MedBridge IT: Prefer token + logs upload. No inbound SSH allowed except from our jump host during maintenance windows.

Ravi (FieldTech): Token works. High level: we need GPU drivers (NVIDIA), container runtime, K8s version, and certain outbound egress. Minimal tested matrix: driver >= 520 + CUDA 11.8 OK, but recommend driver >= 535 + CUDA 12.1 for newest weights and perf patches. If using Ampere or Hopper GPUs, kernel 5.15+ strongly recommended.

Priya (SE): K8s compatibility: we support 1.23 - 1.27 in practice; recommend 1.24-1.26 for the POC to match our CI. kubelet and kube-proxy should match control plane. CRI: containerd 1.5+ acceptable, 1.6+ preferred. If they have Docker, confirm they expose cgroups v1 vs v2 (we prefer cgroup v2).

Ravi (FieldTech): Required components: nvidia-driver (RPM/DEB), nvidia-container-toolkit, the NVIDIA device plugin (daemonset), and NodeFeatureDiscovery for GPU labeling. Also enable hugepages if using certain models (we'll add a note).

Nina - MedBridge IT: We're on RHEL 8.8, driver team manages kernel modules. Secure boot is enabled by policy. Any concerns?

Ravi (FieldTech): With secure-boot on, vendor-signed drivers or you must sign modules. We can provide guidance but signing is on your infra team. If that's a blocker, use a signed kernel/drivers from your vendor or temporarily disable secure-boot during install window. We'll include commands to check signature state.

Priya (SE): Network: Outbound HTTPS (443) to api.redwood.ai and auth.redwood.ai for control-plane callbacks. DNS for *.redwood.ai must resolve. If they block egress, we can do air-gapped install but that's a longer path and needs offline artifacts. Also add: allow access to our S3-compatible endpoints for artifact pulls (we'll provide URLs in the ticket).

Theo (AE): What about key management for the control plane? They asked if keys are stored.

Priya (SE): For Private installs, keys remain in customer control by default. We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and on-prem HSM). We'll attach a one-pager for the security team.

Ravi (FieldTech): Small preflight commands — have them run and paste output:
```
$ uname -a
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv
$ lsmod | grep -i nvidia || echo "nvidia module missing"
$ sudo systemctl status containerd || sudo systemctl status docker
$ kubectl version --short
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
$ curl -I https://api.redwood.ai
```

Nina - MedBridge IT: Running now, sending outputs shortly.

infra-bot: Artifact pull endpoint whitelisted for medbridge-poc: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/medbridge (expires in 48h).

Nina - MedBridge IT: Pasted summary (redacted):
```
Linux host-01 5.19.0-60.el8.x86_64
NVIDIA-SMI 535.86 Driver Version: 535.86 CUDA Version: 12.1
nvidia module present
containerd.service - active (running)
Client Version: v1.25.0
Nodes: 4 Ready
curl: HTTP/2 200
```

Ravi (FieldTech): Looks good. Next: storage and local disk layout. We request at least one NVMe per GPU or a fast local SSD for model shards; recommend 200GB/GPU for multi-billion parameter models. Also ensure IO scheduler is tuned (noop or none) for NVMe.

Priya (SE): Pod scheduling: they'll need to allow our inf-serving DaemonSet to tolerate or not block taints on GPU nodes. We typically use tolerations for gpu=true taint. We'll provide the YAML snippet.

Theo (AE): Can we give them a terse doc for their security team about the installer token lifecycle?

Ravi (FieldTech): Sure: tokens are scoped, single-use for bootstrap, expire 72 hours by default, and are audited. We log token usage and can revoke early. We'll include instructions to generate an extension request.

Priya (SE): Follow-ups I will add to the ticket: Dedicated sizing note (we recommend 1x A100 for heavy concurrent workloads, 2x A10 for cost-sensitive bursty loads), fallback Hosted API key example with cURL for control callbacks, and a link to the private install guide.

Nina - MedBridge IT: One more: Our security team needs to know if the runtime will spawn privileged containers.

Ravi (FieldTech): We avoid privileged containers. The device plugin mounts host devices into containers; some init containers may require CAP_SYS_ADMIN for device setup, but we document and minimize privileges. We'll include a short privilege table.

Theo (AE): Great. Action items: Priya to post the concise checklist + YAML snippets and host key sample. Ravi to add secure-boot / module signing notes and the privilege table. I'll send this to MedBridge and ask them to paste the command outputs into the ticket. Thanks team :rocket:
